alignments.note: Participle predicated of the written subject.

Supplied noun phrase reaching the verb's object: *openeth* already writes the verb's lexeme, so the noun carries none of it (rule 44), and the run of supplied words stands together doing one office as a single added unit (rule 2). The ASV italics corroborate without deciding (rule 7); the competing reading folds *the eyes of* into the verb as part of its idiomatic rendering.
Anarthrous substantival adjective with the supplied *the*, headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rule 46).
Phrasal verb *raiseth up*; the particle completes the rendering and the head stays on the verb (rule 44).
Anarthrous passive participle with the supplied *them that* and the copula rule 20 leaves with the predicate, headed on the word carrying the lexeme (rules 46, 31).
Participle rendered by the finite verb.
Anarthrous substantival adjective with the supplied *the* (rule 46).

review_notes: *the eyes of* is one added unit: it is a contiguous run of supplied English doing one office, and the verb's own lexeme is already written by *openeth* (rules 2, 44).
Each colon writes its subject, so the participles take no supplied relative here.
